body:
Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The big story this weekend is a boil water notice in parts of Bear Valley Springs, issued after power shutoffs disrupted the community's water system — we have the details below. Closer to home, a south Bakersfield neighborhood woke up to shell casings and questions after shots were reported overnight, and fire crews stayed busy from Ridgecrest to east Bakersfield. It's a warm one ahead: near 90 this afternoon, air quality sitting at a healthy 38, and no weather alerts anywhere in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's largest police response came out of south Bakersfield, where several callers reported gunfire near a court in the 900 block of Karma Court. Officers were told to broadcast for officer safety as they headed in, and once on scene they found a shell casing on the north side of the court. A witness told them two men had already left the area on foot to the north, and no victim was ever located. It's the kind of call that ties up units for a while — a perimeter, a search, a report — and ends without an arrest.

Fire ran alongside the police work all night. Crews were sent to a structure fire at a 1,500-square-foot single-story home on West Moyer Avenue in Ridgecrest, where the first engine arrived to find nothing showing and took command; a second engine was diverted from a call on Highway 14 to help, and the response drew a full assignment of engines plus a battalion chief. In east Bakersfield, crews answered a structure fire reported behind a home in the 1000 block of Sumner Street, with two engines, a truck and a rescue assigned. Grass and lot fires kept other units moving around the county.

Officers also worked a robbery at a mini mart in the 3300 block of Wible Road, where a man in a white shirt and red pants ran off on foot with cash and a metal rod; a person was found nearby shortly after. A fight reported in front of a home in the 2700 block of Whitley Drive drew a caller's estimate of about 40 juveniles, one person with a cut above an eyebrow, and a neighbor's report of ATVs, fireworks and possible gunshots in the area. A vehicle struck a pedestrian on Fremont Street, and a foot chase through the alleys between Lincoln, Quincy and Baker streets ended with one person in custody and a perimeter held for another.

The log filled in around those calls: just after 7 p.m., a man under the influence was lying in front of a dentist's office on the 2200 block of Niles Street and refusing to leave; twenty minutes later, a caller asked officers to check on a 13-year-old reportedly left alone for a week at a home on the 400 block of Willow Drive; and a crash involving a car carrying an infant and a toddler came in around 8:13 p.m.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 90 degrees today and a low around 59 tonight. It's currently 66 degrees at Meadows Field, so the morning is comfortable before the heat builds this afternoon. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is good — an AQI of 38, which is about as clean as the valley gets. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. If you're spending the day outside, the early hours are your friend; by mid-afternoon it will feel more like late summer than mid-October.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that a boil water notice has been issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues.** Residents in the affected areas are being told to boil their water before drinking or cooking until the notice is lifted. It's a familiar and frustrating sequence in the mountain communities — shutoffs meant to reduce wildfire risk knock out the pumps and treatment that deliver safe water, and the people who live there absorb the inconvenience. If you have neighbors in Bear Valley Springs, it's worth checking on them today.

**According to 23ABC, hundreds of people gathered Saturday at the Liberty Bell in downtown Bakersfield for a "No Kings" vote-early event ahead of the election.** Organizer Audrey Chavez described it not as a protest but as a celebration of the right to vote, part of a nationwide effort. People began arriving at 9 a.m., then walked over to the Kern County Elections Department to drop off ballots, with organizers saying they wanted residents to understand the process and have their questions answered. One attendee, David, told the station he came because he believes the country is in trouble and wants people to make their voices heard. The gathering at Truxtun and Chester avenues was one of many held across California in the days before the election.

**23ABC also reports that Foothill High School's football team has forfeited all seven of its wins after the California Interscholastic Federation ruled two players ineligible.** Athletic Director Mike Biezard told the station the players were initially deemed eligible, but the school received a letter from the CIF on Tuesday reversing that, forcing the forfeits. Biezard said schools don't verify the residential information parents and guardians provide — the CIF does. It remains unclear why the CIF opened its investigation, and the district is withholding further detail to protect the privacy of the boys and their family. A Foothill kicker told 23ABC it isn't right to ruin a season this way, and community members are unhappy that the whole team is paying the price.

**KGET 17 reports that Friday's East Bakersfield–Foothill game was stopped before halftime because of a medical emergency on the East High sideline.** The Trojans led 17-0 with under two minutes left in the half when play halted; an ambulance drove onto the track near the 40-yard line, followed by Kern County Fire Department vehicles. A Foothill player and someone on East's sideline told the station a member of the visiting staff had collapsed, though authorities have not confirmed that or released any information on the person's condition. After the ambulance left, players, cheerleaders and coaches from both teams gathered at midfield to pray. The game was declared final with Foothill winning — a result the Trojans badly needed, since they must win their last two games to reach the playoffs.

**KGET 17 also reports that a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to the California Highway Patrol.** Few details were immediately available, and the investigation is ongoing. It's a reminder of how quickly things change for people walking along the county's busier roads, and we'll pass along more as it comes.

## Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival turned an ordinary Bakersfield parking lot into a gallery this weekend, with local artists and neighbors working side by side to fill the pavement with color. Events like this don't happen by accident — they take organizers, sponsors and a lot of willing hands — and the result was a space that people who might never set foot in a museum could walk through and enjoy for free. If you stopped by, you saw the best version of this town: creative, unpretentious, and happy to share.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy week at City Hall. The Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets the same day at 2 p.m. Also Tuesday at 2 p.m. is a special meeting of the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee — a good one to watch if you care about bike lanes, sidewalks or how the city moves people around. On Wednesday, October 21, the City Council holds two sessions: a 3:30 p.m. meeting and the regular 5:15 p.m. meeting, both worth checking for the full agendas.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. Tonight, Sunday, October 18, Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour to the Fox. Monday, October 19, the Cults & Classics series screens "Psycho." Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour on Wednesday, October 21. Henry Cho brings "The Empty Nest Tour" on Friday, October 23, and Fred Armisen closes out the week Saturday, October 24, with "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome." And if you're already thinking ahead, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are on sale now.

Have a good Sunday, and stay cool out there.

top.title: Boil water notice issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues
